Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — open live thread for follow-ups from today's all-hands about mission, positioning, and competitors. I'll answer quick clarifications as I can. :wave:

Samir Patel: Quick one — when we say "unified inference across environments", are we telling customers to pick Redwood over cloud-managed endpoints or alongside them?

Avery Chen: Short answer: both. We position Redwood as the fast path for predictable latency + cost and as the orchestration layer for hybrid setups. For enterprises that already built on cloud endpoints, we sell the operational wins (cost predictability, rollouts, SLAs).

Maya Lopez: Follow-up — how prescriptive should sales be on model choices? e.g., recommend quantization vs different model family?

Avery Chen: Recommend patterns, not single models. We provide playbooks: workload types -> suggested families, quant profiles, and routing policies. Sales can lean on those playbooks + benchmark data.

Jordan Kim: From eng's POV: any change to prioritization for runtime optimizations this quarter? Still latency-first?

Samir Patel: We keep latency SLOs for interactive, cost targets for batch. Q2 focus: kernel perf for long-contexts and faster cold-starts for private deployments.

Priya Nair: Competitor angle — customers ask how we compare to big cloud AIs. What's the one-line we should use in demos?

Avery Chen: One-liner: "Redwood gives you cloud-like APIs with enterprise controls and the economics of a production-first serving runtime — predictable latency, transparent cost, and straightforward private deployments."

Samir Patel: Also remind customers about our Quality/Observe hooks — eval-driven regressions are a practical differentiator.

Maya Lopez: Any guidance on messaging for startups vs enterprise? Different assets?

Avery Chen: Yes — startups: speed-to-value + easy API + free credits. Enterprise: security, SLAs, dedicated capacity, and migration playbook.

Priya Nair: Noted. I'll update the battlecard and ping folks for quotes.

ops-bot: Recording & slides uploaded: https://redwood.internal/ah/2028-02-10/recording

Avery Chen: Thanks — keep questions here and we'll turn the top ones into an FAQ. Closing the thread in ~10m for edits. :thumbsup:
